title: Database Management Systems (DBMS) & SQL
desc: Foundational & Advanced DB architecture, Normalization, SQL, Transactions, Concurrency & Indexing
topics: ANSI/SPARC 3-schema architecture (physical, conceptual, external view), physical vs logical data independence, DBMS vs file processing system advantages.
Entity sets, simple vs composite, single vs multivalued, stored vs derived attributes; relationship cardinalities (1:1, 1:N, M:N), participation constraints (total vs partial), weak entity sets.
Relational schema, tuples, attributes, domains; super key, candidate key, primary key, alternate key, foreign key and composite keys.
Domain constraints, entity integrity (no null PK), referential integrity (foreign key constraints), NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, ON DELETE / ON UPDATE CASCADE.
Functional dependencies (FDs), trivial vs non-trivial FDs, Armstrong's Axioms (reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity), attribute closure calculation, finding candidate keys.
First Normal Form (atomic values), 2NF (no partial dependency), 3NF (no transitive dependency), Boyce-Codd Normal Form (every determinant is superkey), lossless join & dependency preservation.
DDL: CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE TABLE vs DELETE; DML: INSERT INTO, UPDATE, DELETE FROM; Data types (VARCHAR, INT, DATE, DECIMAL).
SELECT, DISTINCT, WHERE, ORDER BY (ASC/DESC), aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX), GROUP BY clause, HAVING vs WHERE clauses.
INNER JOIN, LEFT (OUTER) JOIN, RIGHT (OUTER) JOIN, FULL (OUTER) JOIN, CROSS JOIN (Cartesian product), NATURAL JOIN, SELF JOIN with table aliases.
Single-row vs multi-row subqueries, IN, ANY, ALL operators, correlated subqueries, EXISTS vs NOT EXISTS; CREATE VIEW, updatable views vs read-only views.
Transaction lifecycle (Active, Partially Committed, Committed, Failed, Aborted); Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability; failure and rollback mechanisms.
Concurrency anomalies (dirty read, unrepeatable read, phantom read, lost update); conflict serializability, precedence/serialization graph, view serializability.
Shared (S) vs Exclusive (X) locks, Two-Phase Locking (2PL: growing & shrinking phase), Strict 2PL, Rigorous 2PL, Timestamp ordering protocol, Thomas Write Rule.
Primary, secondary, clustered vs non-clustered indexing, dense vs sparse index; B-Tree & B+ Tree structure and search complexity; log-based recovery (WAL, checkpoints).

title: Operating Systems (OS)
desc: Process Lifecycle, CPU Scheduling, Synchronization, Deadlocks, Virtual Memory & File Systems
topics: OS roles, batch, multiprogrammed, time-sharing, distributed, hard vs soft real-time systems; user mode vs kernel mode, mode bit, trap/interrupt vector.
System call interface, categories (process control: fork, exec, wait, exit; file management; device management; information; communication).

Program vs Process, Process Control Block (PCB) fields (PID, registers, PC, scheduling info, memory limits), context switching overhead, 5-state process lifecycle (New, Ready, Running, Waiting, Terminated).
Process vs Thread, User-level threads vs Kernel-level threads, many-to-one, one-to-one, many-to-many models, multithreading benefits and race hazards.
Preemptive vs Non-preemptive scheduling; CPU utilization, throughput, turnaround time, waiting time, response time calculations.
First-Come First-Served (FCFS, convoy effect), Shortest Job First (SJF - optimal for waiting time), Priority Non-Preemptive; Gantt charts & average waiting time.

Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF), Preemptive Priority, Round Robin (RR, time quantum trade-offs: too large = FCFS, too small = context switch overhead), Multilevel Queue & Multilevel Feedback Queue.
Critical Section Problem criteria (Mutual Exclusion, Progress, Bounded Waiting); race conditions; Peterson's solution for two processes; TestAndSet instruction.
Counting vs Binary semaphores, wait() / P() and signal() / V() operations; Producer-Consumer (Bounded Buffer), Readers-Writers problem, Dining Philosophers problem.
Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait; Resource Allocation Graph (RAG) with single vs multiple instances; cycle detection.
Deadlock prevention (attacking each of 4 conditions); Deadlock avoidance: Safe state, Banker's algorithm (Allocation, Max, Available, Need matrix calculations).
Wait-for graph (WFG) for single-unit resources, Deadlock detection algorithm, recovery via process termination (abort all vs abort one-by-one) and resource preemption.
Fixed vs dynamic partitioning, internal vs external fragmentation, compaction; Paging hardware, Page Table, Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB), Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT).
Segmentation architecture, segment table, base and limit registers; Virtual Memory, Demand Paging, page fault service routine.
FIFO page replacement (Belady's Anomaly), Optimal Page Replacement (OPT), Least Recently Used (LRU); Thrashing, working set model, page fault frequency.
File allocation (contiguous, linked, indexed), Inodes; Disk scheduling algorithms: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN (Elevator), C-SCAN, LOOK, C-LOOK head movement calculations.

title: Computer Networks & Internet Protocols
desc: OSI 7-Layer, TCP/IP Suite, Hardware, IPv4/IPv6, CIDR Subnetting, TCP/UDP & Routing
topics: LAN, MAN, WAN, PAN, SAN; topologies (Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, Tree, Hybrid) pros/cons, link calculations (Mesh links = n(n-1)/2), cable fault isolation.
Guided (Twisted pair UTP/STP, Coaxial, Fiber Optic: single vs multimode) vs Unguided media; Circuit switching vs Packet switching (datagram vs virtual circuit).
Physical (bits), Data Link (frames), Network (packets), Transport (segments), Session, Presentation, Application layers; duties, headers, encapsulation & decapsulation.
4-layer and 5-layer TCP/IP models, comparison with OSI model, protocol mapping across layers, port numbers vs IP addresses vs MAC addresses.
Repeater, Hub (active vs passive, collision domain), Bridge, Layer-2 Switch, Layer-3 Switch, Router, Gateway, Modem, Access Point, NIC.
Collision Domains vs Broadcast Domains & VLANs
Collision domains vs broadcast domains per device (Hub = 1 CD / 1 BD; Switch = N CDs / 1 BD; Router = N CDs / N BDs), VLAN segmentation basics.
32-bit IPv4 structure, dotted-decimal notation, Class A, B, C, D (multicast), E (reserved) ranges, default subnet masks, usable host formulas (2^H - 2), private IP ranges.
Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR /n notation), subnetting calculations: network ID, first host, last host, broadcast address, FLSM vs VLSM.
128-bit address format, 8 groups of 4 hex digits, zero compression (::), unicast, anycast, multicast (no broadcast in IPv6), header simplicity vs IPv4.
Transport Layer: TCP vs UDP Headers
Connection-oriented vs connectionless; TCP header (20-60 bytes, SEQ, ACK, flags: SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH, URG, window size) vs UDP header (8 bytes: sport, dport, length, checksum).
Client-Server connection establishment (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), Sequence & Acknowledgment number increment rules; 4-way termination (FIN, ACK, FIN, ACK).
Flow control: Sliding window protocol, Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat ARQ; Congestion control: Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, Fast Recovery.
DNS (port 53), DHCP (ports 67/68), HTTP (80), HTTPS (443), FTP (20/21), SSH (22), Telnet (23), SMTP (25), POP3 (110), IMAP (143), SNMP (161).
Routing Algorithms: Distance Vector vs Link State
Intra-domain vs inter-domain routing; Distance Vector Routing (Bellman-Ford algorithm, count-to-infinity problem, split horizon) vs Link State Routing (OSPF, Dijkstra algorithm).

title: Data Structures & Algorithms (Core & Advanced)
desc: Arrays, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, Hashing, Trees, Heaps, Graphs, Sorting & Complexities
topics: Big-O (worst-case upper bound), Big-Omega (lower bound), Big-Theta (tight bound); space and time complexity calculation, recursion tree & Master Theorem basics.
Row-major order address formula: Base + ((i - L1)*C + (j - L2))*size; Column-major order address formula: Base + ((j - L2)*R + (i - L1))*size.
Node structure, pointer manipulation, insertion, deletion, searching, traversal; time complexity comparisons with arrays; cycle detection (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare).
LIFO principle, push, pop, peek; applications: function call stack, balanced parentheses, infix to postfix conversion, postfix evaluation using stack.
Queues: FIFO, Circular Queue, Deque, Priority Queue
FIFO principle, enqueue, dequeue; linear queue overflow vs circular queue (rear = (rear + 1) % capacity); Double-ended queue (Deque); Priority queue concepts.
Hash functions (division, mid-square, folding); collision resolution: separate chaining vs open addressing (linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing); load factor alpha.
Searching Algorithms: Linear vs Binary Search
Linear search O(n); Binary search O(log n) on sorted arrays, search space reduction, recurrence relation T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1).
Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, Merge Sort (divide-and-conquer), Quick Sort (partitioning, pivot choice), Heap Sort; Best/Avg/Worst time and auxiliary space comparison.
Tree terms (height, depth, leaf, internal node), full, complete, perfect binary trees; Inorder (Left-Root-Right), Preorder, Postorder, Level-order (BFS) traversals.
Binary Search Trees (BST): Search, Insert & Delete
BST property, search O(h), insert O(h), delete node with 0, 1, or 2 children (replace with inorder predecessor/successor), minimum/maximum element.
Balance Factor = Height(Left) - Height(Right) in {-1, 0, +1}; LL, RR, LR, RL rotations for rebalancing after insertion; O(log n) guaranteed search time.
Complete binary tree property, Min-Heap vs Max-Heap array representation (parent = (i-1)/2, left = 2i+1, right = 2i+2), Heapify O(n), insert O(log n), extract-max O(log n), Heapsort O(n log n).
Adjacency matrix vs Adjacency list (space & lookup trade-offs); Breadth First Search (Queue-based) O(V+E), Depth First Search (Stack/Recursion-based) O(V+E), cycle detection.
Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG), Topological sort (Kahn's algorithm using in-degrees), Dijkstra's single-source shortest path algorithm (greedy, non-negative edge weights).
Spanning tree concept (V vertices, V-1 edges, connected acyclic); Prim's algorithm (cut-based greedy) vs Kruskal's algorithm (edge-based greedy with Disjoint Set Union).

title: OOP, Programming Fundamentals & Software Engineering
desc: OOP Pillars, Constructors, Memory Model, Exceptions, SDLC Models, Agile, Testing & Git
topics: Primitive vs non-primitive data types, type casting, operator precedence; Memory layout of a program (Code segment, Data segment, BSS, Heap, Stack).
Classes as blueprints, object instances, data hiding, access modifiers (public, private, protected), getters & setters, encapsulation benefits.
OOP Core: Inheritance Types & Diamond Problem
Single, multilevel, multiple, hierarchical, hybrid inheritance; the diamond problem in multiple inheritance and virtual base classes.
Compile-time (function & operator overloading) vs Run-time polymorphism (function overriding); virtual functions, pure virtual functions, abstract classes, Virtual Method Table (vtable) & vptr.
Default, parameterized, copy constructor; constructor overloading; destructor execution order; shallow copy (pointer copy) vs deep copy (duplicate memory allocation).
Pointers vs references, pointer arithmetic; dynamic allocation (malloc/calloc/realloc/free vs new/delete); memory leaks, dangling pointers, wild pointers.
Try, catch, throw, throws, finally blocks; built-in vs custom exceptions; Multithreading concepts: thread lifecycle, race conditions, critical sections, synchronized blocks.
SDLC Traditional Models: Waterfall to Spiral
Software Development Life Cycle phases (Requirements, Design, Coding, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance); Waterfall, V-Model, Prototyping, Spiral model (risk-driven).

Agile manifesto (4 core values, 12 principles); Scrum roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Dev Team), artifacts (Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Increment), ceremonies (Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Review, Retrospective).
Software Requirements Specification (SRS) qualities (correct, unambiguous, complete, verifiable, traceable); Coupling vs Cohesion; SOLID design principles.
Software Testing Levels & Verification vs Validation

Unit testing, Integration testing (Top-down, Bottom-up, Big Bang), System testing, Acceptance testing (Alpha vs Beta); Verification (Are we building the product right?) vs Validation (Are we building the right product?).
Black-Box vs White-Box Testing & Cyclomatic Complexity
Black-box techniques: Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis (BVA); White-box: Statement, Branch, Path coverage; McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity V(G) = E - N + 2P.
Corrective, adaptive, perfective, preventive maintenance; Git commands: init, clone, add, commit, push, pull, branch, merge, rebase, resolving merge conflicts.

title: Computer Organization, Architecture (COA) & Microprocessors
desc: Number Systems, Logic Gates, CPU Architecture, Addressing Modes, Cache Memory & 8085/8086
topics: Signed magnitude, 1's complement, 2's complement representation, ranges for n bits, arithmetic addition/subtraction, overflow detection; IEEE 754 floating point format (Single: 1 sign + 8 exp + 23 mantissa).
Boolean laws, De Morgan's theorems, SOP and POS forms, universal gates (NAND, NOR); Karnaugh Maps (K-Maps) minimization for 2, 3, 4 variables, don't care conditions.
Half Adder, Full Adder (sum and carry equations), Multiplexer (MUX, data selector: 2^n to 1), Demultiplexer, Encoders, Priority Encoders, Decoders (n to 2^n).
Latches vs Flip-flops; SR, JK (race-around condition, Master-Slave JK), D, T flip-flops, excitation tables; Shift registers; Synchronous vs Asynchronous (Ripple) counters.
Von Neumann vs Harvard architecture, CPU components: ALU, Control Unit, Registers (PC, IR, MAR, MDR, AC, Flags); Instruction cycle: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Interrupt.
Immediate, Direct (Absolute), Indirect, Register, Register Indirect, Indexed, Relative (PC-relative), Base-register, Auto-increment/decrement addressing modes with effective address formulas.
Registers, Cache, Main Memory, Secondary Storage latency/speed pyramid; Cache hit, cache miss, hit ratio, miss penalty; Effective memory access time formula.
Direct mapping (Tag, Line, Word offsets), Fully associative mapping (Tag, Word offsets), K-way Set-Associative mapping (Tag, Set, Word offsets); Tag comparisons & line calculation.
Write-Through (write to cache and RAM simultaneously) vs Write-Back (dirty bit, write to RAM on eviction); Cache replacement: LRU, FIFO, Random; Compulsory, Capacity, Conflict misses.
Programmed I/O, Interrupt-driven I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA controller, burst mode, cycle stealing), Bus arbitration techniques.

8085 8-bit architecture, functional units, internal registers (Accumulator A, B, C, D, E, H, L, Stack Pointer SP, Program Counter PC), Flag register (Sign S, Zero Z, Auxiliary Carry AC, Parity P, Carry CY).
Pin diagram overview: ALE, IO/M, RD, WR, Ready, Reset; Addressing modes (Immediate, Register, Direct, Indirect, Implicit); Instruction categories (Data transfer, Arithmetic, Logical, Branching).

Hardware interrupts priority: TRAP (non-maskable, highest), RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5, INTR; vectored vs non-vectored interrupts; 8086 16-bit architecture overview: BIU vs EU, 6-byte instruction queue, 1MB segmented memory.

title: Information Security & Cryptography
desc: CIA Triad, Malware, Phishing, Firewalls, IDS/IPS, Symmetric & Asymmetric Crypto, PKI & TLS
topics: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Non-Repudiation, Authenticity; Threat vs Vulnerability vs Risk vs Exploit; Principle of Least Privilege, Defense in Depth.
Virus (boot sector, file, macro), Worm (self-replicating over network), Trojan horse, Spyware, Ransomware, Adware, Rootkit, Keylogger, Botnet & Zombies, Logic Bomb.
Phishing, Spear Phishing, Whaling, Vishing, Smishing; Denial of Service (DoS) & Distributed DoS (DDoS): SYN Flood, UDP Flood, Smurf Attack, HTTP Flood mitigation.

Discretionary (DAC), Mandatory (MAC, Bell-LaPadula), Role-Based (RBAC), Attribute-Based (ABAC); Authentication factors (Something you know, have, are), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Biometrics, SSO.
Packet filtering firewalls (stateless), Stateful inspection firewalls, Application proxy firewalls, Next-Gen Firewalls (NGFW); IDS vs IPS: Signature-based vs Anomaly-based detection.

Full backup, Incremental backup, Differential backup (speed vs restore time trade-offs), 3-2-1 backup rule; Incident Response phases: Preparation, Detection, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, Post-Incident.
Plaintext, Ciphertext, Symmetric key; DES (64-bit block, 56-bit key, 16 Feistel rounds), Triple DES (3DES); Advanced Encryption Standard (AES: 128, 192, 256 bits, 10/12/14 rounds, SPN structure).

Public Key vs Private Key; Diffie-Hellman key exchange; RSA algorithm (prime numbers p, q, n=p*q, phi(n)=(p-1)*(q-1), choose e, compute d = e^-1 mod phi(n), encryption c = m^e mod n, decryption m = c^d mod n).
Hash properties: One-way property (pre-image resistance), Second pre-image resistance, Collision resistance, Avalanche effect; MD5 (128-bit, broken), SHA-1 (160-bit), SHA-256, SHA-512; HMAC.

Digital signature process (hashing message, encrypting hash with sender's private key, recipient decrypts with sender's public key); Digital Certificates, X.509 standard, Certificate Authority (CA), CRL, OCSP.

SSL/TLS architecture; TLS 1.3 handshake (negotiating cipher suites, server certificate validation, key exchange, establishing symmetric session key); HTTPS (HTTP over TLS port 443), SSH, IPsec (AH vs ESP).

title: Web Technologies, APIs & Cloud Infrastructure
desc: Client-Server, HTML5/CSS, HTTP Methods & Status Codes, REST APIs, Cookies, OWASP & Cloud Models
topics: Client-server 3-tier enterprise architecture (Presentation, Application/Business logic, Database layer); Web server (Apache, Nginx) vs Application server (Tomcat, Node.js).
HTML5 semantics (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer>); CSS Box Model (content, padding, border, margin), CSS Flexbox vs CSS Grid layouts.
HTTP 1.1 vs HTTP/2 (multiplexing, header compression) vs HTTP/3 (QUIC/UDP); Methods: GET (idempotent, safe), POST, PUT (idempotent), DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS.

2xx (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content); 3xx (301 Moved Permanently, 302 Found, 304 Not Modified); 4xx (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found); 5xx (500 Internal Error, 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable).
REST architectural constraints: Client-Server, Stateless, Cacheable, Uniform Interface, Layered System; JSON format (syntax, data types, key-value pairs, nested objects/arrays).
HTTP statelessness; Cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite flags); Server sessions vs client session storage; LocalStorage vs SessionStorage; JSON Web Tokens (JWT: Header, Payload, Signature).
SQL Injection (parameterized queries/prepared statements), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS: Stored, Reflected, DOM; input sanitization & CSP), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF tokens), CORS policy.
Cloud Computing Models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS

NIST cloud characteristics (On-demand self-service, Broad network access, Resource pooling, Rapid elasticity, Measured service); Service models: IaaS (AWS EC2), PaaS (Heroku, App Engine), SaaS (Gmail, Salesforce); Shared responsibility.
Public, Private, Hybrid, Community, Multi-Cloud; Virtualization: Type-1 Bare-Metal hypervisors (ESXi, Xen) vs Type-2 Hosted hypervisors (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation); Virtual Machines.
Docker containers vs VMs (shared OS kernel, lightweight); Microservices vs Monolithic architecture; High availability, horizontal vs vertical scaling, Load balancers; Disaster Recovery (RPO vs RTO).

title: Banking IT, Payment Systems, CBS & NPCI Architecture
desc: Core Banking (CBS), NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, Payment Cards, ATM/POS, NPCI & RBI Cyber Guidelines
topics: CBS fundamentals, centralized database, branch automation, 24x7 real-time transaction processing; leading CBS software in Indian banks: Finacle (Infosys), BaNCS (TCS), Flexcube (Oracle).
National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT): RBI operated, half-hourly batch settlement (DNS - Deferred Net Settlement), 24x7x365 availability, no minimum or maximum limit, IFSC code routing.
Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS): RBI operated, continuous real-time gross settlement, high-value interbank transactions (Minimum ₹2,00,000, no upper ceiling), 24x7x365 availability.
Immediate Payment Service (IMPS): NPCI operated, real-time 24x7 instant interbank fund transfer via mobile/internet, Mobile Money Identifier (MMID), account + IFSC transfer mode.
UPI architecture: Virtual Payment Address (VPA), 2-factor authentication, single-click 2FA, PSP apps, NPCI switch; UPI 2.0 (overdraft, mandate/autopay), UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay for feature phones.
Payment Cards: Debit, Credit, EMV Chip & Tokenization

Debit vs Credit vs Prepaid cards; Magnetic stripe vs EMV Chip & PIN (microprocessor security); CVV/CVV2; RBI Card-on-File (CoF) Tokenization guidelines (device-specific tokens replacing 16-digit PAN).
ATM & POS Networks & National Financial Switch (NFS)
Automated Teller Machine (ATM) hardware components, Point of Sale (POS) terminals; National Financial Switch (NFS) operated by NPCI for domestic ATM interoperability and switching.
NPCI Ecosystem Products (NACH, AePS, BBPS, FASTag)
National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) establishment (RBI + IBA); NACH (bulk clearing), AePS (Aadhaar Enabled Payment System, biometric banking), BBPS (bill payments), NETC FASTag.
Banking Regulatory Compliance: KYC & AML Basics

Know Your Customer (KYC): Customer Identification Procedure (CIP), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), e-KYC via Aadhaar, C-KYC; Anti-Money Laundering (AML) principles, suspicious transaction reporting (STR).
RBI Cybersecurity Framework for Banks & CERT-In
RBI circular on Cyber Security Framework in Banks: CISO appointment, Security Operations Center (SOC 24x7), baseline cyber controls, incident reporting within specified hours to RBI & CERT-In.

AI/ML use cases (algorithmic fraud detection, automated credit underwriting, AI chatbots); Blockchain & Distributed Ledger Technology in trade finance; Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC - Digital Rupee / e-Rupee).

title: Prelims Master Curriculum: Quantitative Aptitude
desc: Simplification, Number Series, Arithmetic Topics, Quadratic Equations, Data Interpretation (DI)
topics: BODMAS rule, fraction-to-percentage conversions (1/2 to 1/20), squares up to 50, cubes up to 30, square root & cube root tricks, surds & indices.
Arithmetic difference, double difference, multiplication/division patterns, prime numbers, n^2 + 1, n^3 - 1, alternate series identification.
Base change concepts, successive percentage changes (a + b + ab/100), ratio division, mean proportion, third proportion, weighted averages.
Cost price, Selling price, Marked price, Profit%, Loss%, Discount%, successive discounts, dishonest shopkeeper problems.
SI formula (PRT/100), CI formula (P(1 + R/100)^T), difference between CI and SI for 2 years (P(R/100)^2) and 3 years, half-yearly and quarterly compounding.
Efficiency method, total work LCM approach, alternate day work, negative work in pipes (inlet vs outlet / leak), man-days-hours formula (M1*D1*H1/W1 = M2*D2*H2/W2).
Average speed formula (2xy/(x+y)), relative speed (same direction vs opposite direction), train crossing pole/platform, boat upstream (u - v) vs downstream (u + v).
Standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0, sign comparison technique (+ +, - +, + -, - -), factoring without formula, comparing roots of x and y (x > y, x < y, x >= y, CND).
Data Interpretation: Tables, Bar, Line & Pie Charts
Table DI calculation speed, single & double bar graphs, line charts, single & multi-pie charts (degree to percentage: 360 deg = 100%), percentage increase/decrease questions.
Paragraph-based caselet DI (Venn diagram based caselets, equation-based caselets, missing data tables), data sufficiency questions in Quant.

title: Prelims Master Curriculum: Reasoning Ability
desc: Inequalities, Syllogisms, Blood Relations, Direction, Seating Arrangements & Puzzles
topics: Direct statement inequalities (>, >=, =, <=, <), priority rules, open gate vs closed gate method, 'Either Or' conditions, coded inequalities.
Venn diagram method, statements (All, Some, No, Some Not), 'Only a few A are B' (Some A are B and Some A are not B), possibility conclusions, 'Either Or' complementary pairs.
Standard family tree diagrams, 3-generation problems, coded blood relations; Direction & distance sense: 8 directions, Pythagoras theorem, shadow-based problems.
Letter-number-symbol series, step movements (5th to the right of 12th from left), total persons = Left + Right - 1, person interchange positions.
Word comparison coding (Chinese coding), letter shift patterns, number/symbol based new pattern coding decoding.
Single row facing North, facing South, mixed facing North-South; Parallel rows facing each other with 10-12 persons.
Circular table all facing center, all facing outward, mixed facing; Square & Rectangular table arrangements (corners vs sides).
Building floors (1 to 8), vacant floors; stacking boxes one above another, conditional positioning (3 boxes between A and B).
Days of the week (Monday to Sunday), Months with 30/31 days, 2 dates per month (e.g., 7th and 14th of 4 months), Year and age calculation puzzles.
Step-by-step shifting, sorting (numbers descending, words alphabetical); Critical reasoning: Statement & Assumption, Statement & Conclusion, Cause & Effect, Course of Action.

title: Prelims Master Curriculum: English Language
desc: Grammar Rules, Error Detection, Cloze Test, Para Jumbles, Reading Comprehension (RC)
topics: Singular/plural nouns, neither...nor, either...or, not only...but also, along with, as well as, collective nouns, each/every rules.
Present, past, future tenses, past perfect with 'before/after', conditional clauses (If + simple present, will + V1; If + past perfect, would have + V3), modal verbs.
Definite (The) vs indefinite (A, An) articles, omission of articles; prepositions of time (at, on, in), place, direction, fixed prepositions with verbs and adjectives.
Finding grammatical errors across sentences, parallelism rules, pronoun antecedent agreement, dangling modifiers, misplaced adverbs.
Identifying highlighted phrase errors, selecting grammatically correct and contextually appropriate replacements from options.
Reading passage flow, understanding context/tone, eliminating options based on part of speech, collocations, phrasal verbs.
Finding the opening/independent sentence, identifying noun-pronoun links, mandatory pairs, chronological connectors, concluding sentences.
Financial & banking editorial passages (The Hindu / Economic Times), main idea identification, factual questions, inference/tone questions, vocabulary in context.

title: Mocks, PYQs Marathon & Interview Mastery
desc: Timed Test Sprints, Memory Papers, 20-30 Page Revision Pack & Technical Interview Bank
topics: Attempt full 120-minute timed Prelims mock (150 Q: English, Reasoning, Quant); record section scores, time spent, and calculate baseline accuracy.
Core IT Mains Mock #1: DBMS, OS & Networks (50 Q)
50-Question timed technical test; tag errors by concept gap vs calculation vs guess; log into error notebook.
Systems Mains Mock #2: DSA, OOP, SE & COA (50 Q)
50-Question timed test on algorithms, programming, memory, software engineering and digital logic.
Specialist IT Mains Mock #3: Security & Banking IT (50 Q)
50-Question timed test covering CIA triad, cryptography, PKI, CBS, NEFT/RTGS, UPI, and payment security.
Solve 100 actual memory-based questions from past 5 years of IBPS SO IT Officer exams; audit frequent patterns.
Ten full-length 120-minute Prelims mocks attempted with strict sectional timing; aim for consistent 75%+ accuracy.
Professional Knowledge Mains Mocks #1 to #10 (60 Q / 45 Min)
Ten full-length Mains mocks mirroring official exam interface; simulate high-pressure question selection.
Reattempt all incorrect and guessed questions from mock error logs after 48 hours and again after 7 days; verbalize reasoning.
Condense full 6-month syllabus into a 20-30 page master booklet: formulas, port numbers, protocols, SQL syntax, OS algorithms.
Technical Interview Question Bank: Core CS & Banking IT
Prepare explanations for: Normalization, ACID, deadlock conditions, TCP handshake, RSA vs AES, CBS architecture, UPI switch, project defense.
Interview Personal Deliverables (60s Pitch & 'Why Banking IT?')
Master 60-second introduction, 2-minute architectural project explanation, 5 STAR situational examples, and 'Why IT Officer in a Bank?'.
